title: Game Design
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

program.section_heading: Game Design  - Associate of Arts Degree and Certificate of Achievement
outcomes: Build, test, and document analog and digital prototypes based on theory-driven design techniques.
Apply the principles of modern game development through the creation of creative assets and supporting materials.
Contribute to working games and prototypes require team management, effective planning, communication, time management, and responsiveness.
Develop and integrate content that contributes and adds value to games projects or portfolio.
Create modern portfolio demonstrating viable capability utilizing games and class projects.

notes: The page prints one combined section for the degree and the Certificate of Achievement; the certificate shares the single Course Requirements list (27 units) and the single Program Learning Outcomes list, which are recorded here.

Headings are inconsistent: the page heads the program both as 'Associate of Science Degree and Certificate of Achievement' and 'Associate of Arts Degree and Certificate of Achievement', and the closing paragraph refers to an Associate of Science Degree. The certificate requirements are unaffected, but a reviewer may want to confirm the degree type.
Course codes are printed with hyphens (e.g., GAM-3B); they are taken to match the closed-list codes (e.g., GAM 3B).
Outcome 3 is copied as printed, including the wording 'prototypes require team management'.
No general education pattern applies to the certificate; the degree's GE requirement is mentioned only generally.
